requirements.title: Eight-Site Network Scope
requirements.definition: Defines which eight project sites are represented by the financial model, using the Business Case site list as the authoritative network.
requirements.boundary_note: Site selection is separate from the capex, revenue, and operating-cost calculations because the network can change without prescribing those financial assumptions.

requirements.title: Capital Expenditure Model
requirements.definition: Models site-level and program-wide capital expenditures, including midpoint site estimates and separate shared-cost, management, contingency, and reserve line items.
requirements.boundary_note: Site capex and program-wide shared costs are attributes of one total-capex mechanism; operating costs and revenue projections have independently changing assumptions and remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Multi-Stream Revenue Forecast
requirements.definition: Forecasts the network's distinct revenue streams, including parking, pods, fleet contracts or subscriptions, digital-platform income, and ancillary income.
requirements.boundary_note: The individual revenue streams are drivers within one revenue-forecast mechanism rather than separate Requirements; the availability-payment mechanism is separate because it has its own sizing targets and case comparison.

requirements.title: Program Operating Cost Forecast
requirements.definition: Models operating costs for the full network using the client-confirmed CAD 30–40 million annual program-level range rather than the incomplete appendix estimate.
requirements.boundary_note: This Requirement owns the independently selected program operating-cost basis; capital expenditures and revenue drivers can change without changing this assumption.

requirements.title: Financing and Debt Model
requirements.definition: Models the project capital stack, debt schedule, debt service, and debt performance using the streamlined client-approved financing structure.
requirements.boundary_note: The 70/30 debt-equity split, approximate six-percent debt cost, and single-tranche treatment are attributes of one financing mechanism; availability-payment sizing remains separate because it responds to financing outputs rather than defining the debt structure.

requirements.title: Availability Payment Sizing and Justification
requirements.definition: Compares user-funded and PPP cases, demonstrates that user fees alone do not make the project viable and bankable, and sizes availability-style payments to satisfy debt-service and equity-return targets.
requirements.boundary_note: Case comparison, user-fee insufficiency, target DSCR, target equity IRR, and payment sizing are tightly coupled acceptance criteria of the core availability-payment mechanism.

requirements.title: Canadian Tax and CCA Model
requirements.definition: Models Canadian taxation and depreciation using applicable Capital Cost Allowance classes so that tax shields and equity returns are represented credibly.
requirements.boundary_note: CCA treatment has its own accounting rules and independently affects tax shields and returns, so it is separate from the financing and capex mechanisms.

requirements.title: Integrated Financial Statements
requirements.definition: Provides integrated financial statements and cash-flow outputs that connect the model's operating, investment, and financing calculations.
requirements.boundary_note: Financial statements are an independently reviewable output of the model rather than an attribute of any one revenue, cost, or financing module.

requirements.title: Financial Sensitivity Analysis
requirements.definition: Evaluates model outcomes under changes to material drivers such as traffic, occupancy, capex, interest rates, and operating costs.
requirements.boundary_note: The listed sensitivity variables are parameters of one scenario-testing mechanism, not separate Requirements.

requirements.title: CAD 2026 Model Basis
requirements.definition: Expresses the model in Canadian dollars using a 2026 base year.
requirements.boundary_note: Currency and price-base year are tightly coupled global presentation conventions; they are not merged into a specific forecast module because they apply across the model.

requirements.title: Data and Formula Integrity
requirements.definition: Ensures model inputs, formulas, links, and resulting figures are internally consistent, credible, and free from material errors.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a product-quality behavior concerning calculation correctness, not a generic testing or debugging process Requirement; presentation clarity and assumption traceability are independently assessable and remain separate.

requirements.title: Assumption and Source Traceability
requirements.definition: Clearly annotates provisional assumptions and enables material figures to be traced to their underlying inputs, sources, or backing calculations.
requirements.boundary_note: Traceability is independently reviewable even when calculations are correct; the detailed backing tabs are an implementation approach rather than separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Understandable and Auditable Model
requirements.definition: Presents the model through a simplified, professional, and easy-to-follow structure while retaining accessible backing detail for audit and review.
requirements.boundary_note: Front-facing simplicity and access to detailed support are coupled aspects of one layered model structure; dashboard content is separate because its decision metrics can succeed or fail independently.

requirements.title: Government Decision Dashboard
requirements.definition: Provides a clear dashboard summarizing project returns, debt performance, viability, bankability, and other information needed by government decision-makers.
requirements.boundary_note: Dashboard communication is independently testable from the correctness of the underlying calculations and from general workbook navigation.

requirements.title: Government Investment Narrative
requirements.definition: Communicates a clear investment story showing project viability, bankability, and attractiveness rather than presenting calculations without decision-oriented interpretation.
requirements.boundary_note: This Requirement concerns interpretation and narrative across outputs; the numerical availability-payment proof and dashboard metric display remain independently assessable Requirements.

requirements.title: Friday Initial Delivery
requirements.definition: Provides the initial model deliverable by the client's requested Friday deadline.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a bounded delivery obligation rather than a persistent behavior of the financial model.

unresolved_candidates.description: A separate short presentation file may have become an independent deliverable, but the client primarily requested a simpler and clearer model and did not clearly accept a standalone presentation specification.

The proposed Case C, tapered availability payment, corridor levy, refinancing, and anchor-tenant scenarios were freelancer suggestions explicitly described as not yet in the model; no client acceptance establishes them as Requirements.
